deep.reconstruction:
Setting (my reading). V and V' are two potentials defined in all of space (integration element dS = dx dy dz). Each satisfies Poisson's equation with the same density k, ΔV = ΔV' = −4πk, and behaves like a monopole at infinity: V ≈ a/r, V' ≈ b/r. The page proves the reciprocity relation ∫ k (V − V') dS = 0 by applying Green's first identity twice, once with the roles of V and V' exchanged. The previous page is a variational ('Hamiltonian') formulation of an aether/gravitation theory in which V enters with the term 4π dm. This page is the potential-theory lemma serving it, presumably to handle the term ∫V(ΣΔη' + 4π dm). The next page (spherical trigonometry) is unrelated.

Step 1 (integration by parts, Green's first identity). The page writes
∫ ∇V·∇V' dS = ∬ V (V'_x dy dz + V'_y dx dz + V'_z dx dy) − ∫ V ΔV' dS.
In modern form: ∇V·∇V' = div(V∇V') − VΔV', followed by the divergence theorem.

Step 2 (surface element). Write dy dz = cos(x,p) ds, dx dz = cos(y,p) ds, dx dy = cos(z,p) ds. Here p is the normal to the bounding surface, taken inward, which accounts for the overall minus sign. This gives
= −∬ V [V'_x cos(x,p) + V'_y cos(y,p) + V'_z cos(z,p)] ds − ∫ V ΔV' dS.

Step 3 (normal derivative). Since cos(x,p) = ∂x/∂p etc., the chain rule gives
= −∫ V ∂V'/∂p ds − ∫ V ΔV' dS.

Step 4 (exchange V and V'). By the same identity with the roles swapped,
= −∫ V' ∂V/∂p ds − ∫ V' ΔV dS.
The author states this directly, by symmetry of the left-hand side.

Step 5 (data at infinity). The surface is a sphere of radius r → ∞, with
- V = a/r and V' = b/r there;
- ds = r² dφ, where dφ is the element of solid angle, total 4π;
- ∂r/∂p = cos(r,p);
- a marginal note reads ∂V'/∂p = b/r² (sign and cos factor omitted).

Step 6. The surface integrand is then V ∂V'/∂p ds = (a/r)(∓ b cos(r,p)/r²)(r² dφ) = ∓ ab cos(r,p) dφ / r.
- Riemann writes −∫₀^{4π} ab cos(r,p) dφ / r.
- This is O(1/r) and vanishes as r → ∞ (implicit; mine).
With ΔV = ΔV' = −4πk, the two expressions become −∫₀^{4π}(…)dφ/r − ∫4πk V dS and −∫₀^{4π}(…)dφ/r − ∫4πk V' dS, as written on the page.

Step 7. Equating the two expressions and letting r → ∞ gives
∫ 4πk (V − V') dS = 0.
This is Green's reciprocity relation ∫ V ΔV' dS = ∫ V' ΔV dS for the whole of space, specialised to equal sources. (If the struck-out symbol was meant to distinguish densities k, k', the general form ∫ k V' = ∫ k' V results by the same argument.)
errors: Sign of the volume term. With ΔV' = −4πk, the term −∫ V ΔV' dS equals +∫ 4πk V dS, but the page writes −∫ 4πk V dS (and likewise for V'). The slip occurs identically on both sides, so the final relation ∫k(V−V')dS = 0 is unaffected.

Marginal note ∂V'/∂p = b/rr. Correctly, ∂V'/∂p = −(b/r²) cos(r,p) (with sign depending on normal orientation). The page itself later reinstates the cos(r,p) factor. The term vanishes as r → ∞ in any case.
The intermediate line −∫₀^{4π} a·?·dφ/r is garbled or incomplete in the image. It is superseded by the next line, −∫ ab cos(r,p) dφ / r.
The vanishing of the boundary term as r → ∞ is not stated explicitly; it is implied by the 1/r factor.

Regularity (V, V' smooth and decaying like 1/r with gradients like 1/r²) is assumed tacitly. The result is in any case trivial: V − V' is harmonic and decays, hence identically zero. The argument is therefore a roundabout but correct use of Green's identity.

results.modern_name: Green's second identity / Green's reciprocity theorem

results.what: For two potentials of the same density, ∫k(V−V')dS = 0
results.modern_name: Reciprocity / uniqueness lemma for Poisson's equation

deep.surprise_reason: Standard Green's-theorem manipulation, of the kind Riemann used routinely (Dirichlet principle; lectures on gravity, electricity and magnetism ed. Hattendorff). It is a supporting lemma for his aether variational principle and contains nothing non-standard.

checkable.asserts: a/r is harmonic away from the origin (equals 0).

transcription_corrections: The marginal insertion over V' reads approximately '∂V'/∂p = b/(rr)'. It is an annotation and its sign is incomplete.
In 'ΔV' = ΔV = −4π [struck] k', a crossed-out symbol precedes k (possibly a k' or 'dm'). The final result uses the same k for both.
The line '−∫₀^{4π} aφ ∂φ / r' is doubtful: likely 'ab ∂φ/r' or an incomplete expression. The struck-out text before it reads approximately '∫ ab ∂s cos(r,p)/r'.
In the last-but-one line the struck-out symbol before '4πkV dS' is an overwritten character, not part of the formula.
In the swapped line the first second derivative has a stray mark ('∂²V^x/∂x²'); read ∂²V/∂x².
∂s denotes the surface element and ∂S (Riemann's script S) the volume element; φ is the solid angle (limits 0 to 4π).
